children: will be announcing earnings results this Monday after market hours. Here’s what to look for.

Lucid beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $405.3 million, up 56.2% year on year. It was a slower quarter for the company, with a significant miss of analysts’ EBITDA estimates and a significant miss of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Lucid a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Lucid’s revenue to grow 17.7% year on year, slowing from the 68.3% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Lucid has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Lucid’s peers in the automobile manufacturing segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Rivian delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 38.3%, beating analysts’ expectations by 4.8%, and Mobileye reported a revenue decline of 2.4%, topping estimates by 3.2%. Rivian traded up 6.2% following the results while Mobileye was down 15.6%.

Investors in the automobile manufacturing segment have had fairly steady hands going into earnings, with share prices down 1.7% on average over the last month. Lucid is down 12.9% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $7.39 (compared to the current share price of $3.30).
